title: EPA Air Quality System (AQS) Data Mart API
agency: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Office of Air Quality Planning and Standards
questions: annual mean PM2.5 by county in a state
ozone levels at monitors in a state over the last decade
daily PM2.5 during a wildfire smoke episode
air quality monitors in a county

manual.how: Without a key: download EPA's pre-generated files at https://aqs.epa.gov/aqsweb/airdata/download_files.html (annual_conc_by_monitor_<year>.zip, daily_<param>_<year>.zip; unzip and upload the CSV), or use https://www.epa.gov/outdoor-air-quality-data (Download Daily Data). With a key: the links in manual_download/INSTRUCTIONS.md, after replacing {API_KEY} with the key and {AQS_EMAIL} with the email it is registered to (or run the download script with both variables set).

cache.why: Data are revised as agencies certify them; data/ is reused only within a run.

redistribution.why: AQS data are U.S. government works in the public domain (17 U.S.C. 105); the AQS API terms limit request volume, not reuse of the data.

citation: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, Air Quality System (AQS) Data Mart, {dataset}, aqs.epa.gov/data/api, retrieved {retrieved_long}.
clarify: Which pollutant and statistic (annual mean, 98th percentile, 4th-highest 8-hour ozone)? Each standard uses its own statistic.
All monitors or one value per county? Counties often have several monitors and POCs; say how they are combined.
Certified data only? The latest months are not yet certified and arrive about 6 months late.
